Subject: MAP: CrestBank evaluation & security gating (SOC 2 / DPA)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — CrestBank is ready to spin up a short evaluation. Attached is our initial MAP workbook (see CrestBank_MAP_v1.xlsx) with the compliance gates we need to close to move to procurement: SOC 2 evidence, SIG/CAIQ mapping, DPA redlines, and a clear data retention / deletion policy for cardholder and audit logs.

Two clarifying asks from our side before we build the internal acceptance checklist:
- Can Redwood provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II report and a SIG/CAIQ self-assessment for the hosted product?
- Data residency: we need confirmation whether data for EU cardholders can be kept in an EU-only region during evaluation and production. If not, what options exist (Dedicated / Private)?
- DPA: we have a handful of redlines around data subject rights, retention limits, and key management — attaching our proposed redlines in the MAP workbook.

Our target close window: POC (2 weeks) starting 7/1, acceptance decision by 7/21. Procurement would like all security gates cleared or a documented mitigations plan before contract signature.

Can you confirm which artifacts you can share now and who our technical contact should work with for KMS/retention questions?

Best,
Elena
Director, Vendor Risk
CrestBank

Subject: Re: MAP: CrestBank evaluation & security gating (SOC 2 / DPA)

Elena — thanks for the clear MAP workbook and timeline. We're aligned on the major asks; below is what we can provide immediately and proposed acceptance/close flow.

Immediate artifacts (attached):
- Redwood_SOC2_Type2_2029.pdf (latest Type II report)
- SIG/CAIQ self-assessment link (shared in related_links)
- Draft DPA with tracked redlines (we'll upload a DocuSign-ready redline by EOD tomorrow)

High-level MAP & acceptance checkpoints (proposed):
1) Kickoff & access (week 1): credentials, test data scope, and evidence intake owners
2) Evidence sprint (week 1–2): upload SOC2 artifacts, SIG mappings, security questionnaire answers
3) Technical runway (concurrent): confirm KMS/keys, IP allowlists, and data residency option for EU subjects
4) POC finish & acceptance review (end of week 2): signoff from Security + Procurement or documented mitigations

Data residency and key management options (short):
- Hosted (fastest): multi-region hosting; customers can select EU region for production in most cases but hosted evals default to our US region unless requested; production EU residency available for hosted customers with an SSA
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): can be provisioned in an EU region with customer KMS (CMEK) — recommended for regulated cardholder traffic
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full EU residency and customer-managed keys; longest lead time but meets strict regulatory needs

Retention defaults we apply (we can negotiate in DPA):
- Production user content: 90 days (configurable)
- Backups / snapshots: 180 days
- Audit logs / traceability: 24 months by default (can be reduced for evaluation with documented SOW)

Next steps from our side: Rishi will follow up with the KMS/CMEK and audit-log specifics. Marissa will run the POC logistics and the acceptance checklist. I'll circulate a pre-populated DPA redline via DocuSign later today.

I've attached the SOC 2 report and a short checklist for the evidence sprint. If you want EU-residency for the eval starting 7/1, confirm by EOD 6/19 and we'll request EU cluster provisioning; otherwise we'll proceed with the US eval lane and document mitigation.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this along.

– Kimberly Park
Head of Security Enablement, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP: CrestBank evaluation & security gating (SOC 2 / DPA)

Elena / Kimberly — quick technical follow-ups so we can bake concrete acceptance criteria into the MAP.

KMS & key custody:
- For Dedicated: we support CMEK with customer-owned keys in AWS KMS / CloudHSM. Please indicate if CrestBank requires keys to be rotated by you or if Redwood-managed rotation with customer rotation schedule is acceptable.
- For Hosted: we can offer a Bring-Your-Own-Key flow for some customers; for the eval we'd need to scope that (longer lead time).

Retention & deletion semantics (proposal we can put into the DPA redline):
- Production-level user content: retained 90 days, then soft-delete for 30 days before irrecoverable purge (total 120 days)
- Backups: 180-day retention; immutable snapshots held separately and purged after retention window
- Audit/trace logs: 24 months default; if CrestBank requires shorter windows for evaluation we can set a 90-day evaluation window and document as an exception in the MAP
- Data subject access / erasure: we will honor DSARs per the DPA; deletion requests for production data will follow the purge schedule above unless otherwise specified in contract

Traceability & evidence:
- We will provide: S3 object inventory, KMS key ARN(s), access-control lists for the evaluation environment, and scoped CloudTrail exports for audit review (filtered to the evaluation tenancy).

Open question for CrestBank: do you require escrow / key-recovery for the evaluation, or is a documented mitigation acceptable until production? Please confirm.

I'll add these as acceptance rows in the MAP workbook and flag any items that would extend provisioning timelines.

— Rishi
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
